transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess I came in because, well, my sister and her baby recently moved back home with us. And it's great, really, I love them! But... ever since then, I’ve just been a little more on edge than usual? And maybe a bit down. 

I hate to admit it, but I've been snapping over just really little stuff around the house. And then I end up showing up to my college classes or to the mechanic shop already feeling totally drained. I mean, I’m still getting by! I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. But I have missed a couple of deadlines recently, and I actually had to back out of helping build the theater set because I just couldn’t keep everything straight in my head. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right. Is that the kind of thing I should be bringing up?
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about anything lately?

Um, no, I don't think so. I really try not to be a worrier, you know? I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm panicking or freaking out about the house, because it's definitely not like that. 

I haven't really been anxious about anything specific. It's mostly just feeling a little drained from everything going on, like I mentioned. I'm usually pretty good at just going with the flow and handling whatever comes up at work or school. 

Is it okay if I don't really have any big worries to report? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers and not leaving anything important out.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time since your sister and her baby moved in?

Oh, um... no, definitely not most of the time. I know I said I was feeling a bit down earlier, but I really hope I didn't give the wrong impression. I'm definitely not, like, depressed or anything like that. 

It's just... occasionally? Like, maybe just a little tired-down, not actually sad. I still smile and joke around with my sister and the baby, and I'm still really happy to be around them. I really don't want to make it sound like I'm miserable, because I'm definitely not. 

Is it alright if it's just a little bit of feeling down here and there, and not all the time? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture and not overstating things.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do?

Yeah, I think so! I mean, I'm still doing stuff I like. I still really enjoy hanging out with my friends when I have the time, and working on cars at the shop is still pretty satisfying. 

I guess I haven't had quite as much free time to do *everything* I usually like, just with the baby being here and trying to help out around the house. And, well, I did mention dropping out of the theater set building... but that was just a time management thing, you know? Not because I didn't want to do it. 

So, yeah, I'd say I'm still enjoying things! Does that sound okay? I hope I'm not making it seem like I've just given up on everything, because I definitely haven't.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Um, no, I don't think so. My weight has been really steady, actually. Working at the shop keeps me pretty active, and I'm still eating normally, so I haven't noticed any gaining or losing or anything like that. 

I hope that's a good sign? Like, I try to make sure I'm still taking care of myself even with everything being so busy at home right now with my sister and the baby. Is it okay that my weight hasn't changed? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details and being helpful.
Have you been feeling irritable more often than usual?

Um... well, maybe just a tiny bit? I really hate to admit it, because I love having them here, but... yeah, ever since my sister and the baby moved back home, I guess I have been a little more on edge than usual. 

Just, like, snapping over really little stuff at the house. Nothing major, I promise! Just stupid things. But it kind of leaves me showing up to my college classes or the shop already feeling totally drained. I'm still getting by, I really am, but... well, I have missed a couple of deadlines for school, and I guess that's the real reason I backed out of helping with the theater set. I just couldn't keep everything straight in my head with so much going on. 

I feel really bad about the snapping, though. Is it normal to get a little irritable when a house gets that crowded? I really don't want you to think I'm being a bad brother or a jerk or anything. I'm trying my best to keep it together.
Do you have trouble sleeping at night?

Um, no, my sleep is actually really good! I mean, between working at the shop and trying to keep up with my classes, by the time I finally lay down, I'm pretty much exhausted. So I just kind of crash right away. 

I usually sleep right through the night, too, even if the baby wakes up crying. I'm a pretty heavy sleeper, which I guess is really lucky right now. I hope that's a good thing? Like, at least I'm getting enough rest so I can keep helping my sister out during the day. Is it okay that I don't have any trouble with that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try really hard to just do my part and be helpful, so I don't think I have anything to feel guilty about. I'm doing everything I can to support my sister and still go to work at the shop and show up for my classes. 

I guess I feel a tiny bit bad about snapping sometimes, like I mentioned before, but... I always apologize right away! And I really am trying to be a good brother. I hope you don't think I'm a bad person for getting a little frustrated sometimes. I'm really trying my best to handle it all right. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um, no, not at all! I mean, I know I said earlier that I backed out of helping with the theater set at school, but I really want to be clear about that—it wasn't because I didn't *want* to do it. I still really love building things and working with my hands. It's why I like my job at the shop so much. I just... I just ran out of time and energy with everything going on at the house. 

But whenever I actually get a free second, I still really enjoy all my usual hobbies, like playing video games or just tinkering with my tools. I definitely still look forward to all of that stuff. I hope that's a good sign? Like, that I'm still enjoying things and staying active? I just want to make sure you know I'm not, like, totally giving up on my life or anything. I really am trying hard to stay positive. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
Have you been avoiding any social situations or activities because of your current stress at home?

Um, well, I wouldn't really say I'm *avoiding* things. I'm still going to all my classes and showing up for my shifts at the shop, so I'm definitely keeping up with my main responsibilities! 

I did... well, I guess I have turned in a couple of assignments a little late recently. But just a couple! And, like I mentioned before, I did have to drop out of helping with that community theater set project. It wasn't because I wanted to avoid anyone, though, I just... I just couldn't keep up with everything and still be there to help my sister at home. 

But I'm still working hard and going to school! I hope you can see I'm really trying not to let things slip too much. I mean, it's normal to have to step back from just one extra thing when you get busy, right? Do you think I'm handling it okay? I really don't want to let anyone down.
Are you avoiding social interactions with friends or family outside of work and school?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still talk to my friends when I see them at school, and I'm definitely still talking to my sister and my parents at home. I'm not hiding in my room or anything like that! 

I guess maybe I haven't been going out to hang out as much on the weekends, but... that's just because I'm so busy, you know? With the shop and classes and helping out at the house, I'm just kind of tired by the time I get a break. It's not that I don't want to see people. I really try to be friendly and social when I'm out and about. I just need a little time to catch my breath sometimes. That's okay, isn't it? Like, it's normal to just want to rest at home when you have a lot on your plate? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm shutting people out.
Was there anything else significant that happened in your life around the same time your sister and her baby moved in?

Um, no, not really. I mean, honestly, everything else has been pretty steady. Work at the shop is going well, and school is just... school, you know? 

The only really big change was my sister and the baby moving back in. And like I said, I'm really glad they're here! I want to be a good uncle and a supportive brother. I just... I didn't realize how much the dynamic in the house would shift, I guess. But there weren't any other major events or anything like that. Just trying to adjust to the new normal at home. Does that make sense? Like, is it normal for just one big change to throw you off a little bit, even if everything else is fine? I really hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
Have you been having trouble concentrating on your schoolwork or tasks at the mechanic shop?

Um, no, not really! I mean, I wouldn't say I'm having trouble. I'm definitely still getting my work done at the shop, and my boss hasn't said anything about me messing up or anything like that. I always double-check my work on the machinery because I know how important it is to be safe. 

With school... well, like I said, I did turn in a couple of things a little late, but I still got them done! I guess maybe I have to read things over a second time every now and then, just because there's a lot of noise at home with the baby, but I'm still keeping up. I just try to find a quiet corner when I can. It's totally manageable, really. It's normal to get a little distracted when there's a crying baby around, right? I'm still doing okay overall, don't you think?
Have you been feeling less sensitive to things that normally upset you or make you feel strong emotions?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still feel things just as much as I always have. I'm definitely not numb or anything like that! 

If anything, maybe I've been a little... well, just a tiny bit more sensitive lately? Just with being a little tired from all the changes at home, sometimes little things might get to me just a tiny bit more than usual. But I definitely still care about things and feel happy or sad when I'm supposed to. I'm still me, you know? It's pretty normal to feel things a little more when you're adjusting to a new living situation, right? I'm not acting weird or anything, am I?
How long have you been feeling this way since your sister and her baby moved in?

Um, it's been about a month now. Yeah, right around a month, ever since my sister and the baby moved back into the house. 

I mean, it really hasn't been that long in the grand scheme of things, right? Just a few weeks of trying to figure out the new routine and everything. I'm sure it'll all smooth out soon once we all get used to it. A month isn't too long to still be adjusting, is it? I feel like that's a pretty normal timeline for getting used to a baby in the house, don't you think?
Have you been doing things to avoid thinking about your feelings or the stress at home?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm avoiding anything on purpose. 

I definitely try to stay busy, you know? Like, I'll pick up an extra shift at the shop if they need me, or I'll go for a drive just to get out of the house for a bit, but that's just because I like working and being active. It's not like I'm running away from my feelings or anything like that! I just think it's better to stay productive rather than sit around dwelling on things, right? 

I still love my sister and the baby, and I'm happy they're here. I just... I like to keep my hands busy. That's a good way to handle stress, isn't it? It's better than just moping around, don't you think?
Have you been doing anything to distract yourself from thinking about how you're feeling lately?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I'm distracting myself. I mean, I guess it's kind of like what I was just saying about staying busy? 

I just like to keep moving. Like I said, picking up shifts at the shop or just tinkering with my car, things like that. It's just normal stuff I've always liked doing. I don't think I'm doing it to block out my feelings or anything. I just think it's healthier to focus on positive, productive things instead of, you know, overthinking every little emotion. That makes sense, right? It's pretty normal for guys my age to just want to work and stay active, isn't it? I'm not doing anything wrong by just trying to keep a good attitude about it all, am I?
Are you doing anything to avoid reminders of your current living situation?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm avoiding anything on purpose. 

I definitely try to stay busy, you know? Like, I'll pick up an extra shift at the shop if they need me, or I'll go for a drive just to get out of the house for a bit, but that's just because I like working and being active. It's not like I'm running away from my feelings or anything like that! I just think it's better to stay productive rather than sit around dwelling on things, right? 

I still love my sister and the baby, and I'm happy they're here. I just... I like to keep my hands busy. That's a good way to handle stress, isn't it? It's better than just moping around, don't you think?
Are you doing anything to avoid thinking about your current situation at home?

Um, I feel like you've asked me that a couple of times now... did I say something wrong before? I really don't think I'm avoiding it, I promise. 

Like I was saying, I just keep busy with work and fixing up cars and stuff. I'm not trying to run away from the house or block out what's going on with my sister and the baby. I just figure being productive is the best way to handle things when it gets a little cramped or loud at home. That's what you're supposed to do, right? Just keep your head down and work hard? I'm really trying my best to handle it the right way, I just hope that makes sense.
